key_insight: LabSafety Bench shows that while large language models often detect obvious laboratory hazards, they frequently fail at nuanced, context-dependent risk assessment and mitigation; the benchmark quantifies these gaps across models and settings.
problem_solved: Fills the gap of a standardized, systematic evaluation for LLM performance on identifying hazards and assessing safety risks in scientific laboratory contexts—areas where incorrect guidance can be dangerous.
method: Curate a diverse benchmark of realistic lab scenarios and questions targeting hazard identification, risk assessment, and mitigation reasoning.
Evaluate multiple large language models across these tasks, measuring accuracy, calibration, and failure modes under different prompting and context conditions.
Analyze results to identify common error patterns, sensitivity to context, and how performance scales with model size and instruction style.
impact: Gives AI/ML practitioners a concrete tool and metrics to assess and compare LLM safety in lab-facing applications, informing model selection, fine-tuning, and safer deployment practices.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing dataset creation → tasks (identify, assess, mitigate) → model evaluation → analysis
Bar/line chart comparing model performance across tasks (hazard ID vs risk assessment vs mitigation)
Side-by-side scenario cards showing example prompts with correct vs incorrect model responses and consequences
Error taxonomy heatmap highlighting common failure modes (context confusion, overconfidence, missing mitigation)
paper_title: Benchmarking large language models on safety risks in scientific laboratories
paper_authors: Yujun Zhou, Jingdong Yang, Yue Huang, Kehan Guo, Zoe Emory
